title: Evaluation of glycolytic rates in human hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells after target gene depletion
protocol: Disinfect the UCB bag with 70% ethanol.
Cut the end of tubing to allow UCB flow into a 50 mL tube.
Dilute 1 volume of UCB with 3 volumes of isolation buffer.
Add 15 mL of Ficoll Paque Plus to a new 50 mL tube.
Tilt the tube while slowly layering the diluted cord blood on top of the Ficoll Paque Plus media.
Maintain the interface between the Ficoll Paque Plus and the diluted cord blood without disturbing it.
Conduct density gradient centrifugation in a centrifuge with swinging bucket rotor without brake at 400 × g for 35 minutes at 20°C.
Maintain the temperature between 18°C and 20°C during centrifugation to ensure yield, purity, and viability of UCB MNCs.
Remove the upper layer containing plasma and platelets.
Transfer the mononuclear cell layer undisturbed at the interface to a new 50 mL centrifuge tube using a sterile pipette.
Fill the centrifuge tube with isolation buffer to wash the cells.
Use at least three times the volume of isolation buffer compared to the volume of transferred mononuclear cells.
Suspend the cells in isolation buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 20°C with brake on.
Observe the cell suspension under a microscope with a hemocytometer before centrifugation.
Check the original tube containing Ficoll Paque Plus and cord blood sample if few mononuclear cells are observed.
Remove supernatant after initial centrifugation.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 50 mL isolation buffer.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 20°C to wash cells.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant completely after washing.
Resuspend up to 10^8 cells in 300 μL cold MACS buffer at 4°C.
Proceed with isolation of CD34+ HSPCs.
Resuspend up to 108 cells in 300 μL MACS buffer.
Add 100 μL FcR blocking reagent and 100 μL CD34 MicroBeads to the cell suspension.
Mix well and incubate at 2°C–8°C for 30 min.
Flick the bottom of the tube every 10 min during incubation.
Wash the cells by adding 5–10 mL MACS buffer.
Centrifuge the mixture with break on at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Completely aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL MACS buffer.
Place a MS column in the magnetic field of a MACS Separator.
Rinse the column with 500 μL MACS buffer.
Add cell suspension onto the column and collect the flow-through.
Wash the column with 500 μL MACS buffer.
Collect the flow-through and combine with the unlabeled cells collected in step 15 if needed.
Repeat the wash twice for a total of three washes.
Label a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with “CD34+ cells”.
Remove the column from the MACS separator and place it on the labeled tube.
Add 1 mL MACS buffer onto the column and immediately push the plunger firmly into the column to flush out the labeled CD34+ cells.
Optional: The eluted fraction can be enriched over a second MS Column to improve the purity of isolated CD34+ cells.
Repeat the magnetic separation procedure from steps 14–18 once by using a new column.
Dilute the RetroNectin stock solution (1 mg/mL) with sterilized PBS to achieve a concentration of 50 μg/mL.
Dispense 1 mL of diluted RetroNectin solution (50 μg/mL) into each well of a non-treated 6-well plate with aseptic technique.
Incubate overnight (∼18 h) at 4°C when coating the plate on the day prior to lentiviral transduction.
Aspirate the RetroNectin solution from the plate.
Block the plate with 2% bovine serum albumin (BSA) solution for 30 min at room temperature (20°C).
Remove the BSA solution and add 2 ml of PBS to each well to wash the plate.
Remove PBS but do not allow the plate to dry.
Add 1 ml of lentiviral supernatants to each well of the RetroNectin-coated plate.
Centrifuge the plate at 2000 × g for 2.5 h at 32°C.
Remove the lentiviral supernatant from the plate.
Do not allow the plate to dry.
Treat removed lentiviral supernatants with 10% bleach for at least 30 min prior to disposal.
Pipette 1 × 10^6 CD34+ HSPCs in 2 mL SFEM complete medium into each well of the plate.
Add polybrene to each well to a final concentration of 4 μg/mL.
Centrifuge the plate with break on at 600 × g for 10 min at 32°C.
Incubate the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 48 h.
Change the medium for the transduced cells and add puromycin to a final concentration of 2 μg/mL.
Culture the cells with puromycin for 3–4 days to select successfully-transduced CD34+ HSPCs.
Use approximately 1 × 10^6 transduced cells from each group for protein extraction and Western Blot (or RNA extraction and RT-qPCR) to validate target gene expression knockdown.
Unpack a Seahorse XFe96 sensor cartridge set in the cell culture hood.
Disassemble the sensor cartridge from the utility plate.
Place the sensor cartridge upside down to avoid sensors touching the work surface.
Fill each well of the utility plate with 200 μL Seahorse XF calibrant solution.
Put the sensor cartridge onto the utility plate ensuring sensors are completely submerged in the calibrant solution.
Hydrate the assembled sensor cartridge at 37°C in a non-CO2 incubator overnight (∼18 h).
Verify that the incubator is properly humidified to prevent evaporation of the calibrant.
Turn on the Seahorse XFe96 Analyzer and open the “Wave” software.
Select “Heater on” with the temperature set at 37°C to stabilize the temperature.
Dilute Cell-Tak stock solution with 0.1 M NaHCO3 (pH 8.0) to a final concentration of 22.4 μg/mL.
Prepare 3 mL of diluted Cell-Tak solution for one Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplate.
Apply 25 μL of the diluted Cell-Tak solution to each well of a Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplate and let stand for at least 20 min at room temperature (20°C).
Aspirate the solution from each well after adsorption is complete.
Wash each well twice with 200 μL sterile water.
Coat the Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplate on the day of the Glycolytic Rate Assay and use immediately after coating.
Alternatively, coat the plate in advance and store the coated plate at 4°C for up to one week before using it in the assay.
Warm the coated plate to room temperature (20°C) before cell seeding.
Prepare the assay medium by supplementing Seahorse XF RPMI medium with 2 mM glutamine, 10 mM glucose, 1 mM pyruvate, and 4 mM HEPES.
Warm the assay medium to 37°C in a water bath.
Count each group of lentivirally transduced CD34+ HSPCs three times with an automated cell counter.
Use the average cell number to calculate the volume needed to transfer 1.0 × 10^6 cells of each group to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Count the cell number of each group accurately three times.
Pellet cells at 300 × g with break on for 10 min at room temperature (20°C).
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1.8 mL warm assay medium.
Pipette 180 μL cell suspension to each sample well using an 8-channel multi-pipette.
Add 180 μL assay medium without cells to each background correction well of the Cell-Tak-coated XF96 cell culture microplate.
Maintain a pipetting angle of approximately 45° for even distribution and adhesion of cells.
Centrifuge the plate with break on at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C).
Examine under a microscope to confirm adherence of the cells to the well bottom.
Place the cell culture plate in a regular incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Load the sensor cartridge with assay compounds once it is ready, taking 10–30 minutes.
Move the cell culture plate to a non-CO2 incubator only when the calibration process of the Seahorse Glycolytic Rate Assay is about to start.
Incubate the cells in the non-CO2 incubator for exactly 30 minutes before starting the assay.
Open one foil pack from the Seahorse XF Glycolytic Rate Assay Kit and remove the Rotenone (Rot)/Antimycin A (AA) vial and the 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) vial.
Tap down the vials to ensure the powder is at the bottom before opening them.
Prepare compound stock solutions with assay medium according to the provided table.
Vortex for approximately 1 minute to completely dissolve the compounds.
Dispense 20 μL of Rot/AA working solution into port A of each assay well using an 8-channel multi-pipette and a sterile reagent reservoir.
Avoid residual drops on top of the sensor cartridge.
Visually confirm that the solution has been loaded evenly into the ports.
Align the B/C port loading guide with the cartridge to place the letter “B” in the top left-hand corner.
Dispense 22 μL of 2-DG working solution into port B of each assay well using an 8-channel multi-pipette and a sterile reagent reservoir.
Place the cell culture plate in a non-CO2 incubator for 30 min before being measured in the Glycolytic Rate Assay.
Place the loaded sensor cartridge with the utility plate into the Seahorse XFe Analyzer and start the calibration process.
Replace the utility plate with an XF96 cell culture microplate seeded with CD34+ HSPCs after 30 minutes of incubation in a non-CO2 incubator when prompted.
Begin the assay.
